text.title: DORA + Reliability Metrics Report Core Rules
text.summary: 18 testable rules grounding the dora-metrics methodology. The four DORA metrics, their performance tiers, data sources, and 2025 evolution including a fifth reliability metric and AI code generation impact. Rules for setting up DORA metric collection, tool integrations, and dashboard requirements. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale and is referenced by the decision tree.

rule.statement: Deploy events MUST be ingested in a CDEvents-compatible schema (or equivalent: timestamp, service, env, commit SHA, success bool); ad-hoc CSV is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Without a typed event schema, lead-time/MTTR computation drifts and cannot be reconciled across teams.

rule.statement: Lead Time for Changes MUST be `prod_deploy_timestamp - commit_timestamp` for the latest commit in the deployed SHA; merge-time approximations are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Merge-time hides queueing in CI/CD; commit-to-prod is the true user-felt lead time.

rule.statement: Deployment Frequency MUST be reported as a rolling 7-day count per service; monthly aggregates hide regressions.
rule.rationale: Long aggregation windows mask the very degradation the metric is meant to surface.

rule.statement: Change Failure Rate MUST be computed as `incidents_within_24h / deploys` where incidents reference a deploy commit; opinion polls are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Self-reported CFR is biased low; deploy-linked incident data is the only objective source.

rule.statement: MTTR MUST include detection-to-mitigation, not just response-to-mitigation; clock starts when the incident's first symptom is observable.
rule.rationale: Hiding detection time turns MTTR into a vanity metric that improves while user-visible outage time stays flat.

rule.statement: Report MUST include Reliability (SLO attainment %) alongside the four DORA metrics; the 2024 update positions Reliability as the fifth pillar.
rule.rationale: Pure throughput metrics encourage shipping at the expense of stability; Reliability is the counterbalance.

rule.statement: Measure all four DORA metrics as a set — throughput (DF + LT) and stability (CFR + MTTR) together reveal the full delivery health picture.
rule.rationale: Optimizing only throughput metrics drives risky large batches; only stability metrics drives slow but safe delivery. Elite performers achieve high scores on all four simultaneously.

rule.statement: Track trends, not absolute values — week-over-week improvement matters more than hitting exact elite thresholds.
rule.rationale: Teams in different domains (embedded, banking) have structural constraints that prevent elite DF; improvement trajectory predicts organizational outcomes better than absolute tier.

rule.statement: Add Reliability (SLO achievement rate) as a fifth metric alongside the four core DORA metrics.
rule.rationale: DORA 2025 research shows SLO achievement and error budget consumption predict organizational outcomes independently of the four delivery metrics.

rule.statement: Monitor batch size when using AI code generation tools; expect a ~7% reduction in delivery stability with heavy AI adoption.
rule.rationale: AI-generated code encourages larger commits and pull requests, which violates the small-batch principle underlying elite DORA performance.

rule.statement: Automate metric collection from CI/CD pipelines — never rely on manual reporting.
rule.rationale: Manual reporting introduces lag and bias; teams under pressure stop updating it. Automated collection from deployment events is the only reliable baseline.

rule.statement: Define "production deployment" precisely before collecting data: successful deploy to prod environment, not staging.
rule.rationale: Ambiguous definition inflates DF when staging deployments are counted. The signal must reflect real user impact.

rule.statement: Mark deployments as rollback or hotfix at emit time, not retroactively, so CFR is accurate.
rule.rationale: Retroactive classification is inconsistent across team members; the CI/CD pipeline knows at deploy time whether the trigger was a hotfix branch or rollback workflow.

rule.statement: Link incident records to the deployment that caused them; MTTR without deployment linkage cannot distinguish release-caused incidents from infrastructure failures.
rule.rationale: Only release-caused incidents contribute to Change Failure Rate. Infrastructure-only incidents belong in reliability/SLO tracking, not CFR.

rule.statement: Export deployment events to a Prometheus-compatible endpoint or PostgreSQL from every CI/CD pipeline immediately after each successful deploy.
rule.rationale: Post-hoc scraping of CI/CD logs is fragile; emit events at the point of deployment where all metadata (commit SHA, timestamp, is_rollback) is available.

rule.statement: Review DORA metrics in team retrospectives, never in performance reviews of individual engineers.
rule.rationale: Using DORA metrics to evaluate individuals causes gaming (smaller commits, avoided deployments, suppressed incident reports) that destroys the signal.

rule.statement: Set weekly automated reports; alert on degradation (not on absolute low values) during the first 90 days of collection.
rule.rationale: First 90 days establishes baseline. Early alerting on low absolute values discourages teams before the baseline is known.

rule.statement: If the team has no production deploys yet (pre-product), this methodology MUST be skipped.
rule.rationale: Computing DORA on zero deploys yields noise.

section.title: Background

list.item: Deployment Frequency: Elite = multiple/day; High = weekly–monthly; Medium = monthly–6mo; Low = 6mo+
Lead Time for Changes: Elite = <1 hour; High = 1 day–1 week; Medium = 1–6 months; Low = 6mo+
Change Failure Rate: Elite = 0–15%; High = 16–30%; Medium = 31–45%; Low = 46%+
Mean Time to Restore: Elite = <1 hour; High = <1 day; Medium = 1 day–1 week; Low = 1 week–1 month

section.p: Deployment Frequency: count of successful production deployments per time period. Data: CI/CD pipeline events, deployment logs.
Lead Time for Changes: time from first commit to successful production deployment. Data: Git commit timestamps + CI/CD deployment timestamps.
Change Failure Rate: percentage of deployments requiring rollback, hotfix, or causing an incident. Data: incident tracking system + deployment records.
Mean Time to Restore: average time from incident detection to resolution. Data: incident management (PagerDuty, Opsgenie) resolved timestamps.
Research findings from Accelerate (Forsgren, Humble, Kim, 2018):

list.item: Elite performers are 2x more likely to exceed organizational performance goals
Elite vs low: 208x higher deployment frequency
Elite vs low: 106x faster lead time
Elite vs low: 2,604x faster recovery time
GitLab native: enable DORA analytics (Premium/Ultimate tier) — zero additional tooling
GitHub + any incident tool: Google Four Keys (open source, GCP-native event pipeline)
Multi-platform enterprise: Sleuth, LinearB, or Jellyfish for aggregation
Custom stack: Prometheus + PostgreSQL schema + Grafana dashboard (templates in this methodology)
